IIII.|TO THE ROMANES.|391}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|V|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial V, a grotesque mask and flowers.png|imgsize=155px|fl={{verse|chapter=4|verse=1}}}}VHAT shal vve say then that{{sup|‖}} Abraham did finde, our father according to the flesh? {{verse|chapter=4|verse=2}}† For if Abraham vvere iustified {{sup|‖}} by vvorkes, he hath glorie, but not vvith God. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=3}}† For vvhat saieth the Scripture? {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 5, 6. Gal. 3, 6. Ia. 2, 23.''}}* ''Abraham beleeued God, and it vvas reputed him to iustice''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=4}}† But {{sup|‖}} to him that vvorketh, the revvard is not {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λογίζεται''}}∷ imputed according to grace, but according to dette. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=5}}† But {{sup|‖}} to him that vvorketh not, yet beleeueth in him that iustifieth the impious, his faith is {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''λογίζεται''}}∷ reputed to iustice according to the purpose of the grace of God. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=6}}† {{sup|‖}} As Dauid also termeth the blessednes of a man, to vvhom God reputeth iustice vvithout vvorkes: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=7}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Ps. 31, 1.''}}* ''Blessed are they, vvhose iniquities be forgiuen, and vvhose sinnes be{{sup|‖}} {{sup|‖}} couered''. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=8}}† ''Blessed is the man, to vvhom our Lord hath not imputed sinne''.

{{verse|chapter=4|verse=9}}† This blessednes then doth it abide in the circumcision, or in the prepuce also? For vve say that vnto Abraham faith vvas {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ The word, ''Reputed'', doth not diminish the truth of the iustice: as though it were reputed for iustice, being not iustice in deede. but signifieth, that as it was in it self, so God esteemed & reputed it. as the same greeke word must needes be taken ''v. 4''. next going before, & ''1 Cor. 4, 1''. and els where.}}∷ reputed to iustice. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=10}}† Hovv vvas it reputed? in circumcision, or in prepuce? Not in circumcision, but in prepuce. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=11}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Gen. 17, 10.''}}* he receiued {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Gen. 17, 10. · Our Sacraments of the new Lavv giue ''ex opere operato'' that grace and iustice of faith vvhich here is commended. whereas circūcisiō vvas but a signe or marke of the same.}}∷ the signe of circumcision, {{sup|‖}} a seale of the iustice of faith that is in prepuce: that he might be the father of al that beleeue by the prepuce, that vnto them also it may be reputed to iustice: {{verse|chapter=4|verse=12}}† and might be father of circumcision, not to them only that are of the circumcision, but to them also that folovv the steppes of the faith that is in the prepuce of our father Abraham. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=13}}† For not by the Lavv vvas the promisse to Abraham, or to his seede, that he should be heire of the vvorld: but by the iustice of faith. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=14}}† For if they that are of the Lavv, be heires: faith is made voide, the promisse is abolished. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=15}}† For the Lavv vvorketh vvrath. For vvhere is no lavv, neither is there preuarication. {{verse|chapter=4|verse=16}}† Therfore of faith: that according to grace the promisse may be firme to al the seede, not to that only vvhich is of the Lavv, but to that also vvhich is of the faith of Abraham, vvho is<noinclude>{{rh|||the}}</noinclude>
